correctness.rationale: For K=join_i D_{p_i}, its minimal-nonface graph is a disjoint union of complete components corresponding to block sizes >=2 plus singleton isolates; therefore Aut(K)=S_{m1}×∏_{p>=2}(S_p wr S_{m_p}). Polyhedral products turn joins into Cartesian products equivariantly, so after block-permutation quotients the literal orbit is a product of SP^{m_p}(Y_p). For p>=2, Y_p=Z_{D_p}/S_p is the strict pushout A=SP^p(S1), B=D²×SP^{p-1}(S1), C=S1×SP^{p-1}(S1), where boundary map sends (w,M) to {w}∪M. Compact-to-Hausdorff verifies the repeated-boundary-coordinate quotient. SP^q(S1)→S1 by multiplying coordinates is a homotopy equivalence: unordered roots identify SP^q(C×) with C^{q-1}×C×, and SP^q(S1)→SP^q(C×) is a homotopy equivalence. The attaching H1 matrix [[1,1],[0,-1]] is unimodular, giving π1(Y_p)=0 and reduced integral H3(Y_p)=Z with all other reduced groups zero; simply connected homology-Whitehead gives Y_p≃S³. Taking symmetric powers preserves homotopy equivalence via coordinatewise homotopies; p=1 factors are contractible. For odd-degree generators the S_{m_p} exterior invariants are Q in degree0 and one Q in degree3, and no higher wedges, yielding the exterior ring on distinct p>=2 sizes. Read actual verify.py finite block automorphisms and determinant checks; independently checked matrix determinant -1 and example K=D2 (two solid-torus gluing, S³). No extrapolation from finite experiments is used in the uniform proof.
residual_risks: The proof establishes homotopy equivalence, not homeomorphism, to symmetric powers S³; no integral ring formula for finite symmetric powers. General finite group action includes stabilizers; the rational ring argument uses orbit transfer in characteristic zero. Original 1967 Morton full article was not read, but the required πq map is proved directly using the polynomial-coefficient model.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge after Resultary and primary-literature comparison, the combination of exact wreath-product Aut(K), literal full vertex-permutation orbit space and integral homotopy product of SP^{m_p}(S³) is not implied by the inspected prior results. Morton supplies the homotopy ingredient SP^q(S1)→S1, not the moment-angle orbit-space classification. Bahri–Bendersky–Cohen–Gitler treat symmetric products of polyhedral products in a different functorial role, while Yu and Limonchenko–Solomadin study quotients by torus subgroups, not full permutation automorphism groups. No closely matched covering theorem was found; lack of universal literature access remains a documented priority risk.
